title: Why do people buy gold?
reason: 从昨天的工程风险管理主题轮换到金融经济与资产选择。本集用黄金解释价格波动、危机时期的避险需求、稀缺供给与长期价值，既贴近金融科技背景，也适合联系个人投资判断。练习不追求复杂金融术语，而是通过客观题和逐级撤架的短答反复调用六个高频表达，帮助把能看懂的表达转化为能主动说出的英语。

targetExpressions.meaning: to increase and decrease at different times
targetExpressions.usage: The price of gold can go up and down as demand changes.

targetExpressions.meaning: to reach the highest level ever recorded
targetExpressions.usage: Gold prices hit an all-time high in early 2026.

targetExpressions.meaning: during periods of serious difficulty or uncertainty
targetExpressions.usage: Investors often look for safer assets in times of crisis.

targetExpressions.meaning: to be generally considered or regarded in a particular way
targetExpressions.usage: Gold is thought of as a relatively safe investment.

targetExpressions.meaning: an asset expected to keep its value over time
targetExpressions.usage: Gold is perceived to be a store of value over the longer term.

targetExpressions.meaning: from nothing or without an existing source
targetExpressions.usage: Unlike paper money, gold cannot be created out of thin air.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the price description from the programme: The price of gold has always ________.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says the price of gold has always gone up and down, although it reached its highest ever price in 2026.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence best reflects why people buy gold during uncertain periods?

options.text: Gold is thought of as a safe investment.
Gold is thought from a safe investment.
Gold is thought to a safe investment.
Gold thinks of investors as safe.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme says people buy gold in crises because it is thought of as a safe investment.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the context phrase: People often buy more gold ________, when economies and markets feel uncertain.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript directly links increased demand for gold with times of crisis.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does describing gold as 'a store of value' suggest?

options.text: It is expected to keep value over a longer period.
It can be printed whenever demand rises.
It is connected to only one government.
Its price never changes at all.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Suki Cooper says gold's neutrality means it is perceived as a store of value over the longer term; this does not mean its price never moves.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the supply argument: Gold cannot be created ________ in the way paper money can be printed.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The expert says gold cannot be created or fabricated out of thin air, which limits supply and supports underlying value.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: If a price 'hits an all-time high', what has happened?

options.text: It has reached its highest recorded level.
It has returned to its average level.
It has fallen below every earlier price.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme explains that gold reached its highest ever price in early 2026—its all-time high.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'go up and down' naturally in a reusable work or finance context?

options.text: Transaction volumes go up and down during the month.
The team went the deadline up and down.
We went up and down the incident.
The report is go up and down yesterday.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The phrase naturally describes a quantity that increases and decreases over time, such as prices or transaction volumes.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the perception phrase: Because it is neutral, gold is ________ a store of value over the longer term.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says gold is perceived to be a store of value because it is not tied to one government, economy or market; 'thought of as' expresses the same supported idea.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80-120 words. Use this structure: (1) topic—why gold remains valuable; (2) two key ideas—crisis demand and limited supply; (3) conclusion/example—why physical gold still appeals in a virtual, changing world. Phrase bank: 'in times of crisis', 'a store of value', 'out of thin air'. Use at least two naturally. Simple, accurate English is enough; advanced financial vocabulary and complex sentences are not required.
referencePoints: Gold was historically easier to carry and trade than cattle or timber and remains a financial asset.
People buy gold in times of crisis because it is considered a relatively safe investment.
Gold is not tied to one government, economy or market, so it is perceived as a longer-term store of value.
Gold cannot be created out of thin air; limited supply helps support its underlying value when demand rises.
Gold prices can rise during political or economic uncertainty but still go up and down after reaching a peak.
In a virtual and changeable world, some people value gold because it is physical, solid and dependable.
